To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the uptake of Ni by roots of four plant species varied greatly, (b) the translocation of Ni from roots to shoots varied greatly, (c) the accumulation of Ni by shoots of four plant species differed greatly, and (d) these differences among and within species are important for the tolerance of plants to Ni toxicity.

1) the tolerance of white clover to nickel toxicity depends on its low uptake and translocation of nickel from roots to shoots; 2) the sensitivity of ryegrass to nickel toxicity depends mainly on its high nickel uptake and translocation; and 3) cabbage is relatively sensitive to nickel toxicity because of its relatively high nickel translocation even though it has a low nickel uptake.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a plant species for phytoremediation.
the mechanisms of plant tolerance to Ni toxicity and the potential for using plants to remediate soils with high Ni content.
the development of plants for phytoremediation of high-Ni soils, and the results of this study provide some information on plant differences for tolerance to Ni toxicity.
